extracted.intended_audience: IP office staff, policymakers, patent researchers, patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and methodological notes for interpreting WIPO patent statistics (e.g., patents in force, pendency, PPH flows, utility model and microorganism deposit statistics) across national and regional patent offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees and patent lapse
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent holders must pay maintenance fees to maintain the validity of their patents; depending on technological and commercial considerations, patent holders may opt to let a patent lapse before the end of the full protection term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentages shown (e.g., patents in force as a percentage of total applications in the year of filing) reflect that some patents lapse due to non-payment of maintenance fees. Not all offices provide these data; example: data for 92 offices show 40.3% of applications for which patents were eventually granted remained in force for at least 8 years after the application date, and about 18.1% lasted the full 20-year term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of patents in force calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The average age of patents in force is calculated using the formula: Σ(p*y)/Σp, where p is the number of patents in force and y the number of years between filing and reporting year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this weighted-average formula to compute average patent age at an office. The report provides office-level comparisons (e.g., 2016 vs 2021) but users should note methodological caveats about data harmonization across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of share of applications granted
rubrics_metrics.description: The share of applications granted shown in a given year should not be interpreted as grant rates because they are based on the examination date rather than the date when the application was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of grants in a given year relates to applications filed in previous years. Because the metric is tied to examination/grant dates, comparisons of 'share granted' across offices or over time can be misleading unless the timing issue is accounted for. WIPO collects data using a common questionnaire, but procedural differences between offices prevent full harmonization—exercise caution when comparing offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of pending applications (before examination vs in examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending application data are separated between (a) all patent applications, at any stage in the process, that are awaiting a final decision by a patent office (including those for which applicants have not filed a request for examination), and (b) patent applications undergoing examination for which the applicant has requested examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application processing varies by office: in some offices applications automatically proceed to examination unless applicants withdraw them; in others, applications do not proceed to examination unless applicants file a separate request. Therefore present pending-application counts split into 'before examination' and 'in examination' to account for procedural differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency time metrics (first office action and final decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average pendency times are reported for two milestones: time to first office action and time to final decision (measured in months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendency statistics are office-specific and depend on procedural practices; WIPO warns that differences in patent procedures between offices prevent full harmonization of these measures — exercise caution when making cross-office comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent office examiner resources and experience metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics include the number of patent examiners (FTE) at offices and the average years of experience of examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metrics are intended as indicators of office capacity and institutional knowledge. Differences in reporting, definitions of FTE, and examination models across offices mean comparisons should be interpreted carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) - fast-track mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent prosecution highway is a bilateral agreement between two offices that enables applicants to request a fast-track examination whereby patent examiners can use the work already undertaken by the other office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH data in the report are shown by flows between office of first filing and office of later examination. Note that some entries (marked with an asterisk) may be based on office of earlier examination rather than office of first filing; users should check footnotes when interpreting PPH flow counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microorganism deposit requirement for biotechnology patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits of microorganisms for patent procedures are important for biotechnological inventions; disclosing an invention is a requirement for receiving a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report shows trends and counts of microorganism deposits (by year and by international depositary authority). For biotechnology-related patent filings, a biological deposit may be required to satisfy disclosure obligations; users should consult applicable deposit rules and the listed depositaries (e.g., ATCC, DSMZ).

rubrics_metrics.name: World totals and PCT national phase inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: World totals in the report are WIPO estimates using data covering a subset of offices and include both applications filed directly with national/regional offices and applications entering offices through the PCT national phase (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because not all offices report by origin and coverage varies (e.g., world totals use 82 offices for some series), world-level aggregates are estimates and may omit some jurisdictions; users should consult data-coverage notes and footnotes (e.g., China's pre-2017 data not comparable due to methodology change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data comparability and breaks in series
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in national methodologies (for example, changes in how a large office reports) can create breaks in time series making direct comparisons over time unreliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report highlights specific cases (e.g., China's pre-2017 data are not comparable due to a change in methodology) and advises caution in interpreting growth rates or trend shifts that may be driven by methodological breaks rather than substantive changes.
